Subject: Private deployment onboarding - initial network questions

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're excited to move forward with the private deployment (VPC peering + on‑prem package). Before we schedule the kickoff, our network team asked for a couple of clarifications so we can prepare the diagram and firewall requests: 

- Preferred approach for private endpoints: do you recommend AWS PrivateLink or internal ALB/NLB with peering?
- Required egress port ranges and IPs for outbound telemetry and S3 access (if any).
- Do you provide an install bundle for air‑gapped environments or will we need to arrange external download + transfer?

I've attached a high‑level network diagram and our current proxy/NAT topology. Can you flag anything obvious?

Appreciate it — Jenna

Stellar Medical Devices
jenna.locke@stellarmed.com
(415) 555-0199

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding - initial network questions

Jenna — thanks for the diagram, looks like a good starting point. Short answers up front:

- Private endpoints: we support both PrivateLink and peered VPC endpoints. For most StellarMed customers we recommend VPC peering when low latency and full subnet routing is desired; PrivateLink is good when you want tight control and simplified routing (no cross-AZ route table changes). We'll map this to your security requirements in the kickoff.
- Egress: outbound to our telemetry and package repositories is over TLS 443. IP ranges are 54.227.0.0/16 and 34.210.128.0/17 (we'll provide an allowlist file you can import).
- Air‑gapped install: we have an on‑prem package tarball (see attachment) and an install checklist for transfer via secure media. The installer validates signatures and checksums.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff working session w/ NetOps, CS, and our Integrations engineer (30–45m). Proposed slots: Wed 11/3 10:00 or Thu 11/4 14:00 PT.
2) Pre‑kickoff: Jenna to share any existing peering/Transit Gateway constraints and the attachment you sent (done).
3) We'll send a connectivity checklist and port/IP allowlist prior to the meeting.

I'll attach the install bundle and a short connectivity checklist. Marissa, can you own the kickoff invite and include the runbook link? Monica, please add any compliance notes for air‑gapped installs.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com

From: netops@stellarmed.com <netops@stellarmed.com>

Subject: RE: Private deployment onboarding - initial network questions

Thanks — quick follow up from our NetOps engineers after reviewing the runbook: 

- We prefer peering into a dedicated management VPC behind our firewall (Transit Gateway is in use for other vendors). Confirm Redwood supports peering into a dedicated subnet and accepts NATed egress for updates.
- Can you confirm the TLS certificate expectations for mutual TLS between the on‑prem runtime and Redwood metrics endpoints? We use internal mTLS for outbound vendors.
- In the diagram we see an SSH bastion; does the installer require SSH access to individual nodes post‑install or is it agented and operated via our orchestration only?

Attached is a slightly updated diagram with our MGMT-VPC overlay. We'll bring these points to the kickoff and would appreciate a short checklist for the mTLS cert chain and any CSR template.

Regards,
StellarMed NetOps

Attachments: stellarmed_network_diagram.pdf (updated)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: netops@stellarmed.com <netops@stellarmed.com>, Jenna Locke <jenna.locke@stellarmed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding - initial network questions

Thanks for the updated diagram and questions — short answers and action items below so the kickoff is productive.

- Peering into a dedicated management VPC: supported. We can peer into a /24 or larger subnet; our infra team will provide route table examples. Action: Dylan to share peering template and minimal route table entries by Tue 11/9.
- mTLS: we support mutual TLS for metrics and control-plane traffic. Action: Monica to send CSR template and required cert fields (CN, SANs) and an example chain by Mon 11/8. We'll also include instructions for importing CA bundles into the installer.
- SSH & post‑install access: the on‑prem package is designed to be agented; we do not require SSH into application nodes for regular operations. If you prefer SSH for troubleshooting, we can provide a short diagnostic guide that runs under a locked account that you control. Action: Dylan to attach the diagnostic guide and the signed installer checksum.

I'll also note compliance: for air‑gapped installs we generate a transfer manifest and a signed release bundle; audit hashes are available for evidence. If you have specific evidence requests, include them in the kickoff.

Looking forward to Thu 11/4 — please flag any agenda additions.

Monica Patel
Enterprise Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
